cards.explanation: The answer is True. Paul asks what the advantage of being a Jew is, and he answers fast: "Much in every way." Right after talking about circumcision being a matter of the heart (Romans 2:29), you might expect him to say there's nothing left. He doesn't say that, friends. He says there's plenty, and he's about to start counting.

The answer is that they were trusted with God's very words. Paul says, "First of all, they have been entrusted with the very words of God." Think about being handed the only copy of a treasured family recipe and told to keep it safe. That's a big deal to be trusted with, and Paul puts it first on his list. Notice he says "First of all…" so there's more where that came from.

The answer is Certainly not. Paul asks if their lack of faith will nullify God's faithfulness, then answers in a flash: "Certainly not!" People can drop the ball, and God's faithfulness stays right where it is. Paul keeps going with "Let God be true and every man a liar." That's about as firm as an answer gets.

The answer is that God is proved right and victorious. Paul quotes the Scriptures: "So that You may be proved right when You speak and victorious when You judge." Two things happen in that line, God speaks and God judges, and He comes out on top both times. Paul had just said, "Let God be true and every man a liar." and this line is his backup. No plot twist, no upset, friends.

The answer is False. Paul does not agree that God is unjust. He says, "Certainly not!" He's only trying the idea on, and he marks it with "I am speaking in human terms." Then he shuts it down with a question: "In that case, how could God judge the world?"

The answer is judge. Paul says, "In that case, how could God judge the world?" His point is that God does judge the world, so the idea that He's unjust can't be right. Paul shuts that door in one short question.

The answer is truthfulness. Paul writes, "…if my falsehood accentuates God’s truthfulness, to the increase of His glory, why am I still condemned as a sinner?" It's a falsehood on one side and God's truthfulness on the other. Paul is asking it with himself in the picture. He's pointing out something that doesn't add up.

The answer is "Let us do evil that good may result." Paul says some slanderously claim that we say “Let us do evil that good may result…”. Notice the word slanderously, friends. These people are putting words in his mouth. Then Paul says of them, “Their condemnation is deserved!”

The answer is Jews and Greeks alike. Paul asks, "Are we any better?" and answers, "Not at all." Then he says he's already made the charge that "…Jews and Greeks alike are all under sin." Alike is the key word. Nobody gets an exception.

The answer is False. The quote says, "There is no one who understands, no one who seeks God." There's no "except a few" tucked in there, friends. It stays with the same point as the line before it: "There is no one righteous, not even one."

The answer is that all have turned away. The quote says, "All have turned away, they have together become worthless…" It says all, and it means everybody in the picture. Then it finishes with "there is no one who does good, not even one." Together, that's the whole crowd turning away.

The answer is True. Throats, tongues, lips and mouths all point to speech. The quotes talk about tongues that "practice deceit" and mouths "…full of cursing and bitterness." Four body parts, one theme: words.

The answer is do. The quotes began with throats, tongues, lips and mouths, and now they come to "Their feet are swift to shed blood…" Feet are for going and doing, so this part is about actions. It's a heavy passage, friends, and I think this is the hardest line of the lot to read. First what people say, then what people do.

The answer is the fear of God. The last quote says, "There is no fear of God before their eyes." After the throats, tongues, mouths and feet, this one turns to the eyes. What's missing from that picture is the fear of God. It's the last of the quotes Paul gives.

The answer is so the whole world is accountable to God. Paul says the law speaks to those under it "…so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God." Notice how big that gets, friends: from the people under the law to the whole world. Every mouth silenced, and everybody accountable to God. That's the purpose he gives.

The answer is False. Paul writes, "Therefore no one will be justified in His sight by works of the law." It's a very clear line, and it follows everything he just said about every mouth being silenced. Works of the law can't do it.

The answer is sin. Paul says, "For the law merely brings awareness of sin." The law shows sin for what it is. It does the showing, and Paul doesn't say it does the fixing. Think of it as a smoke detector, friends: it tells you about the smoke, and the fire still needs somebody else to deal with it.
